Lavanya, beta, your father called you lazy today? Come, sit. Let me tell you about when I was nine.
Every evening I dawdled over homework. My father would say, "Anirban, you're lazy. You'll never do anything." After a while I believed him. Why try, if I was just lazy?
Then my uncle came to stay. One evening he pulled a chair beside me and said, "What's the first small thing?" I said, "Copy the question." "Do that. I'll sit here." So I did. Then, "What's next?"
He never called me lazy. He just broke it into little steps and sat with me at the start. I finished that homework, beta. And I stopped believing I was lazy.
